policy: Operationally relevant systems are reviewed across open-source, open-core, source-available, and proprietary source models; licensing is a visible classification, not an inclusion gate.

projects.name: Agno
projects.description: Python framework and AgentOS runtime for building, serving, observing, securing, and managing agent platforms.
projects.canonical_data: agent definitions, sessions, memory, knowledge, traces, evaluations, and application storage
strengths: Covers the full agent-platform path from SDK definitions to API runtime, UI, storage, traces, and deployment
Human approvals, JWT-based access control, memory, knowledge, evaluations, and observability are integrated
Large tool and interface ecosystem with MCP, A2A, messaging, and self-hosted deployment options
weaknesses: The broad SDK, runtime, UI, and deployment surface increases conceptual and upgrade complexity
Default telemetry requires an explicit opt-out for teams with strict outbound-data policies
Application teams still own tool safety, model behavior, infrastructure hardening, and cost controls
projects.why_it_matters: Shows what an integrated, self-hostable agent platform looks like when runtime operations are treated as part of the framework rather than an afterthought.

projects.name: Aider
projects.description: Mature terminal pair-programming agent built around Git-aware edits and broad model support.
projects.canonical_data: Git working tree and commits
strengths: Git-native accountability
Broad model compatibility
Long operational track record
weaknesses: Narrower tool surface than newer harnesses
Primarily an interactive pair programmer
projects.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that constrained, Git-native agency can be both useful and auditable.

projects.name: Browser Use
projects.description: Framework and agent runtime for controlling websites through browsers.
projects.canonical_data: browser state and execution history
strengths: Rich browser automation primitives
Model and browser integrations
Large active ecosystem
weaknesses: Websites remain nondeterministic
Cloud browser paths complicate data boundaries
projects.why_it_matters: A focused reference for agents acting through unstable visual environments.

projects.name: Claude Code
projects.description: Proprietary Anthropic coding agent for terminal, IDE, GitHub, and programmatic workflows.
projects.canonical_data: local working tree, project instructions, and resumable Claude Code sessions
projects.current_repo_note: The public repository is canonical, but the operational distribution remains proprietary under Anthropic commercial terms.
strengths: Strong repository-scale editing, shell use, and Git workflows
Granular permissions, hooks, MCP, subagents, and resumable sessions
Terminal, IDE, GitHub, and SDK surfaces
weaknesses: Operational implementation is proprietary and coupled to Anthropic models
Model processing is remote even though tools and files can remain local
projects.why_it_matters: A major provider-native reference for controlled coding agents and the runtime exposed through Claude Agent SDKs.

projects.name: Claude Agent SDK
projects.description: Provider-native Python and TypeScript SDKs that embed the Claude Code agent loop, tools, permissions, hooks, sessions, subagents, skills, plugins, and MCP.
projects.canonical_data: streamed SDK messages, Claude Code session state, project instructions, checkpoints, tool results, and application-defined external session stores
projects.current_repo_note: The Python repository is the representative open wrapper; the product also ships a commercially governed TypeScript SDK and bundles the Claude Code runtime.
strengths: Exposes the production Claude Code agent loop with built-in file, shell, web, MCP, subagent, skill, and plugin capabilities
Permissions, lifecycle hooks, human input, file checkpointing, session resume and fork, and OpenTelemetry support provide strong control seams
Python and TypeScript bindings let applications own orchestration while reusing a mature interactive coding-agent runtime
weaknesses: The runtime is provider-native and requires Anthropic models rather than a substitutable model backend
The MIT Python wrapper bundles a commercially governed Claude Code executable, while the TypeScript SDK is governed by Anthropic commercial terms
Powerful default file and shell tools require deliberate permission, sandbox, credential, and data-retention policy
projects.why_it_matters: Shows the tradeoff of embedding a mature provider-owned agent runtime: unusually deep tools and controls with materially less model and licensing portability than open provider-agnostic frameworks.

projects.name: Cline
projects.description: IDE-centered coding agent with approval-gated file, terminal, browser, and MCP tools.
projects.canonical_data: working tree and task history
strengths: Excellent approval and diff loop
Broad provider and MCP support
Visible step-by-step execution
weaknesses: IDE-centered workflow
Operator review remains the main safety boundary
projects.why_it_matters: A leading example of human control around autonomous coding tools.

projects.name: Codex
projects.description: Local coding agent for reading, changing, and running code from the terminal.
projects.canonical_data: working tree and session state
strengths: Strong repository-scale execution
Explicit approvals and sandboxing
Terminal, IDE, SDK, and MCP surfaces
weaknesses: Best experience depends on hosted models
Long autonomous runs still require review
projects.why_it_matters: A reference implementation for controlled, tool-using coding agents.

projects.name: CrewAI
projects.description: Framework for coordinating role-based agents and structured multi-agent flows.
projects.canonical_data: application-defined crew and flow state
strengths: Accessible role-based orchestration
Explicit flows complement autonomous crews
Large ecosystem
weaknesses: More agents can amplify nondeterminism
Debugging emergent handoffs remains difficult
projects.why_it_matters: A prominent test case for whether multi-agent structure improves outcomes enough to justify complexity.

projects.name: DB-GPT
projects.description: Agentic data assistant for planning and executing SQL, Python analysis, reusable skills, and multi-source reporting in sandboxed environments.
projects.canonical_data: database schemas, connected datasets, knowledge bases, skills, workflow state, and generated artifacts
strengths: Plans and executes multi-step SQL and Python analysis rather than stopping at query generation
Combines databases, files, knowledge bases, reusable skills, RAG, and multi-agent workflows
Supports sandboxed execution, self-hosting, local models, and OpenAI-compatible providers
weaknesses: The broad platform and deployment surface create substantial setup and operational complexity
Human approval and rollback behavior vary across agents, tools, and application flows
Reliable production analysis still depends on model quality and careful database permissions
projects.why_it_matters: A comprehensive reference for data agents that combine query generation, code execution, skills, sandboxing, and reports in one runtime.

projects.name: DeepSeek Harness
projects.description: Plugin-oriented agent runtime with event-sourced sessions, policy controls, workflows, and replaceable model and tool seams.
projects.canonical_data: append-only session events in JSONL or SQLite plus YAML configuration
strengths: Event-sourced sessions support persistence, replay, forks, search, and telemetry
Model, tool, storage, sandbox, and interface layers are replaceable plugins
Approvals, workflows, background jobs, and subagents are first-class runtime concepts
weaknesses: Upstream labels the project a developer preview with compatibility-breaking changes
The broad plugin surface creates substantial architectural and operational complexity
Some optional subagent integrations depend on separately licensed external runtimes
projects.why_it_matters: A rare open implementation of a durable agent harness where execution policy, event history, recovery, and extension seams are explicit runtime primitives.

projects.name: Devin
projects.description: Hosted autonomous software-engineering agent with an observable shell, IDE, browser, API, and parallel sessions.
projects.canonical_data: cloud workspaces, repository state, session history, knowledge, and playbooks
strengths: Long-running cloud workspaces expose shell, editor, browser, and logs
Human takeover, API access, parallel sessions, knowledge, and playbooks support team workflows
Mature GitHub and Slack integration
weaknesses: Proprietary managed service with limited implementation inspectability
Cloud execution and retained organizational context reduce data sovereignty
Official guidance still recommends bounded tasks and human review for reliability
projects.why_it_matters: A reference proprietary cloud agent for delegated, asynchronous software work rather than only interactive code assistance.

projects.name: DSPy
projects.description: Framework for programming and optimizing modular AI systems, including retrieval pipelines, tool-using ReAct agents, evaluation, and self-improving model programs.
projects.canonical_data: Python modules, declarative signatures, examples, evaluation sets, optimization traces, and compiled programs
strengths: Declarative signatures and modular programs separate system intent from brittle hand-written prompts
Evaluation-driven optimizers can improve prompts, examples, and weights against explicit metrics
Includes tool schemas and ReAct agent loops while remaining compatible with varied model backends
weaknesses: It is a general AI-programming framework rather than a full operational agent platform
Optimization requires representative datasets, metrics, model calls, and careful experimental discipline
Deployment, persistence, permissions, and production recovery remain application-defined
projects.why_it_matters: Broadens the Atlas beyond orchestration by treating AI-system behavior as typed, evaluable, optimizable programs.

projects.name: Gemini CLI
projects.description: Open-source terminal agent for coding, research, and tool-assisted workflows.
projects.canonical_data: working tree and session state
strengths: Broad terminal tool surface
MCP and extension support
Large active community
weaknesses: Centered on Gemini model access
Recovery and trace ergonomics are still evolving
projects.why_it_matters: Shows how a provider-backed terminal agent can remain extensible and open source.

projects.name: Google Agent Development Kit
projects.description: Google's open multi-language framework for tool-using agents, graph workflows, delegation, state, evaluation, human approvals, and local or managed deployment.
projects.canonical_data: code or declarative agent and workflow definitions, chronological session events, mutable state, artifacts, traces, and evaluation sets
projects.current_repo_note: The Python repository is the canonical metadata source for one ADK product also implemented by Google in TypeScript, Go, Java, and Kotlin; language feature parity varies.
strengths: Open, inspectable agent and workflow runtime with official implementations across five languages
Broad tool, MCP, OpenAPI, A2A, state, memory, evaluation, trace, and deployment seams
Callbacks, tool confirmation, workflow interruption, pause and resume, and session rewind provide strong control and recovery surfaces
weaknesses: Feature parity and maturity vary materially by language, with Python providing the deepest implementation
Gemini and Google Cloud are the best-integrated path even though model and deployment seams are replaceable
Major-version changes to agent APIs, events, and session schemas create migration risk in a fast-moving framework
projects.why_it_matters: A significant provider-published framework whose operational runner remains open and replaceable across model, storage, tool, protocol, and deployment seams.

projects.name: Goose
projects.description: Extensible local agent for coding and general computer tasks with MCP-based tools.
projects.canonical_data: working tree and local configuration
projects.current_repo_note: The project moved from block/goose to aaif-goose/goose.
strengths: Local and extensible
MCP-native tool ecosystem
Useful beyond code-only tasks
weaknesses: Reliability varies by extension and model
Observability is less structured than graph runtimes
projects.why_it_matters: A practical model for local, protocol-extensible agents.

projects.name: GPT Researcher
projects.description: Autonomous research agent that gathers web sources and produces cited reports.
projects.canonical_data: research artifacts and generated reports
strengths: Research-specific planning
Cited report output
Multiple deployment surfaces
weaknesses: Source quality still needs human review
Long runs can be costly and difficult to steer
projects.why_it_matters: Separates research-agent evaluation from generic coding autonomy.

projects.name: GStack
projects.description: Cross-host AI engineering workflow with generated skills, browser automation, QA, security, release, and persistent-learning integrations.
projects.canonical_data: Git-versioned skills, plans, review and QA artifacts, browser evidence, and append-only learning records
projects.current_repo_note: Multi-host support is generated from a Claude-oriented canonical skill set; GBrain integration is adjacent and separately cataloged.
strengths: End-to-end, evidence-bearing delivery process from product framing through review, QA, release, and retrospection
Local browser automation, security review, verification gates, and recovery-oriented tooling
Generated support across ten coding-agent hosts plus pair-agent and cross-model review workflows
weaknesses: The large workflow and skill surface is strongly opinionated and requires deliberate adoption
The primary experience remains Claude Code-oriented despite generated multi-host support
A fast-moving main branch, no formal GitHub releases, and partial Windows support increase upgrade risk
projects.why_it_matters: Shows how structured roles, artifacts, safety gates, and verification turn general coding agents into a repeatable software-delivery system.

projects.name: Haystack
projects.description: Production-oriented Python orchestration framework for explicit RAG pipelines, tool-using agents, context engineering, evaluation, and lifecycle control.
projects.canonical_data: typed pipeline graphs, component state, documents, messages, tool calls, traces, and application-defined memory
strengths: Explicit pipelines, loops, branches, routing, retrieval, and agent steps make control flow inspectable
Lifecycle hooks, tool-call metrics, token accounting, evaluation, and tracing support production recovery
Broad provider, retrieval, storage, component, and deployment interoperability
weaknesses: Complex pipelines require more deliberate composition than higher-level opinionated agent APIs
Some serving, MCP, UI, and enterprise operations rely on adjacent Hayhooks or commercial products
Persistent memory and authorization policy remain application and integration concerns
projects.why_it_matters: A mature reference for transparent, production-oriented orchestration where retrieval and agent control flow remain explicit.

projects.name: Kiro
projects.description: Proprietary agentic IDE and CLI centered on specs, steering files, hooks, powers, and MCP integrations.
projects.canonical_data: local working tree plus Markdown specs, steering files, hooks, and service-managed sessions
projects.current_repo_note: Kiro's official GitHub repository is documentation and issue-tracking surface, not reusable operational source.
strengths: Specs and steering keep intent in reviewable project files
Hooks and powers support explicit repeatable automation
IDE, CLI, and MCP cover interactive and scripted workflows
weaknesses: Operational implementation is proprietary and governed by AWS service terms
Model and service processing limits local-only operation
projects.why_it_matters: A distinct provider product that makes specifications and durable project guidance first-class coding-agent artifacts.

projects.name: LangChain
projects.description: Model-portable Python framework with a prebuilt agent loop, composable tools, middleware, structured output, and durable LangGraph execution.
projects.canonical_data: application-defined graph state and message history
strengths: Prebuilt agent loop with composable model, tool, middleware, and structured-output seams
Broad first-party provider integrations and model portability
Durable execution, persistence, and human interruption through LangGraph
weaknesses: The abstraction surface and release cadence create meaningful upgrade overhead
Durability depends on the separate LangGraph package rather than a small standalone core
The strongest hosted observability and deployment paths are separate LangSmith services
projects.why_it_matters: A mature reference for a high-level, provider-portable agent API layered over a durable workflow runtime.

projects.name: LangGraph
projects.description: Graph-based runtime for durable, stateful, controllable agent workflows.
projects.canonical_data: application-defined graph state and checkpoints
strengths: Durable checkpoints and resumability
Explicit human-in-the-loop control
Broad ecosystem interoperability
weaknesses: Framework complexity is substantial
Application quality depends on graph design
projects.why_it_matters: A benchmark for treating control, persistence, and recovery as runtime primitives.

projects.name: Letta Code
projects.description: Stateful agent harness with memory, identity, skills, schedules, subagents, and self-improvement.
projects.canonical_data: database
projects.current_repo_note: The former letta-ai/letta repository is now a landing page; active code moved here.
strengths: Memory and identity are first-class
Git-tracked context
Dreaming, skills, schedules, and subagents
weaknesses: Agent can rewrite its own context
Cloud features affect portability
Current codebase is much newer than historical repo
projects.why_it_matters: Defines embedded, self-editing agent memory and long-horizon runtime behavior.

projects.name: LlamaIndex
projects.description: Data and agent framework for ingestion, indexing, retrieval, tools, workflows, multi-agent applications, and document-centric AI systems.
projects.canonical_data: documents, nodes, indices, workflow events, messages, tool state, and application-defined stores
projects.current_repo_note: This entry represents the MIT-licensed LlamaIndex OSS framework; LlamaParse and LlamaCloud are separate commercial services.
strengths: Deep ingestion, indexing, retrieval, tool, workflow, and document-agent primitives in one ecosystem
Very broad integration catalog across models, embeddings, data sources, and storage backends
Supports high-level agent construction while preserving lower-level control over data and retrieval
weaknesses: The large package and integration ecosystem creates versioning, discovery, and maintenance overhead
Hosted parsing, extraction, indexing, and deployed-agent capabilities are separate commercial services
Application teams must design authorization, durable state, evaluation, and recovery policy
projects.why_it_matters: A foundational framework for data-intensive AI systems where retrieval, documents, structured data, and agents converge.

projects.name: Mastra
projects.description: Open-core TypeScript framework and runtime for tool-using agents, durable workflows, memory, delegation, evaluation, observability, and self-hosted or managed deployment.
projects.canonical_data: application-defined agents, tools, message and thread memory, workflow run state and snapshots, traces, evaluations, and storage records
projects.current_repo_note: The root license path map makes repository content outside ee/ Apache-2.0; every ee/ path is commercially restricted, and Mastra Platform is a separate proprietary service.
strengths: A configurable agent loop backed by typed tools, workflows, memory, scoring, and durable execution
Strong approval, suspension, resumption, tracing, replay, and failure-control surfaces
Broad model portability plus MCP, A2A, ACP, browser, sandbox, storage, and deployment integrations
weaknesses: The large, rapidly changing monorepo creates substantial conceptual and upgrade surface
Production authentication, authorization, Agent Builder, and other ee/ features have commercial restrictions
The documentation license page still broadly describes Mastra as Apache-2.0 despite the authoritative root license carving out every ee/ path
projects.why_it_matters: An unusually integrated TypeScript agent stack that treats tools, memory, workflows, evaluation, human control, observability, and deployment as one operational framework while exposing a clear open-core boundary.

projects.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
projects.description: Framework for building, orchestrating, and hosting agents with workflows and multi-agent patterns.
projects.canonical_data: application-defined workflow and agent state
projects.current_repo_note: Microsoft identifies Agent Framework as the successor path for AutoGen and Semantic Kernel agent APIs.
strengths: Explicit workflows and multi-agent patterns
Strong enterprise observability concepts
Broad .NET and Python integration
weaknesses: Newer consolidated framework
Azure integrations can pull deployments toward one cloud
projects.why_it_matters: Represents the convergence of agent SDKs and durable workflow orchestration.

projects.name: Open Interpreter
projects.description: Local agent that uses code and shell execution to complete computer tasks.
projects.canonical_data: local files and session history
projects.current_repo_note: The canonical repository is openinterpreter/openinterpreter.
strengths: Simple local execution model
Broad model support
Flexible code-driven tool use
weaknesses: Host execution increases risk
Less structured recovery than sandboxed runtimes
projects.why_it_matters: Makes the tradeoff between local control and host-execution safety especially visible.

projects.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
projects.description: Provider-agnostic Python agent framework with tools, handoffs, guardrails, resumable runs, sessions, tracing, MCP, and sandbox integrations.
projects.canonical_data: typed run items, resumable run state, and pluggable session stores
strengths: Small core abstractions cover tools, handoffs, guardrails, approvals, and resumable multi-agent runs
Pluggable sessions, tracing processors, model providers, MCP transports, and sandbox backends
Typed run items and explicit interruption state make execution inspectable and recoverable
weaknesses: OpenAI models and hosted tools remain the most complete and documented execution path
Provider adapters can expose uneven feature support across models
Some tracing, hosted tools, and sandbox paths send data to external services
projects.why_it_matters: Shows how a provider-published SDK can keep its operational loop open while exposing replaceable model, storage, tracing, and execution seams.

projects.name: OpenClaw
projects.description: Local-first personal agent runtime connecting models, tools, skills, schedules, devices, and messaging channels through one gateway.
projects.canonical_data: local gateway sessions, workspace files, skills, configuration, and channel state
strengths: Local gateway unifies sessions, tools, events, channels, and companion devices
Broad provider, channel, skill, plugin, and MCP interoperability
Schedules and persistent workspace state support proactive personal-agent workflows
weaknesses: Host tools and inbound messaging create a large security boundary
Safe multi-user exposure requires deliberate pairing, sandbox, and gateway configuration
Breadth increases operational and troubleshooting complexity
projects.why_it_matters: A prominent open personal-agent runtime whose durable gateway and communication surfaces go well beyond a single coding session.

projects.name: OpenCode
projects.description: Provider-flexible open-source coding agent with terminal and desktop interfaces.
projects.canonical_data: working tree and session state
strengths: Strong model-provider portability
Multiple interfaces
Open extension surface
weaknesses: Fast-moving interfaces can churn
Safety depends on configured tools and permissions
projects.why_it_matters: A strong benchmark for provider-neutral coding-agent design.

projects.name: OpenHands
projects.description: Self-hostable coding-agent platform and control center for interactive work and event- or schedule-driven automations.
projects.canonical_data: working trees, agent sessions, conversation events, and automation definitions
strengths: OpenHands agent plus Agent Canvas support self-hosted interactive and automated work
Agents can run on the host, in containers, on remote machines, or in managed cloud
ACP support allows alternate coding-agent backends
weaknesses: Running without a sandbox grants agent tools the host user's filesystem access
Multiple backends and automation integrations add deployment complexity
projects.why_it_matters: A major open alternative for observable coding agents and for operating several agent backends through one control surface.

projects.name: Pi
projects.description: Minimal, extensible terminal coding agent bundled with a multi-provider API, agent core, and TUI libraries.
projects.canonical_data: local working tree, JSONL sessions, extensions, prompts, and skills
strengths: Small agent loop with first-party libraries for models, state, and terminal UI
Extensions, prompts, skills, and themes make the harness deeply adaptable
First-class Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google model support
weaknesses: No built-in permission system for filesystem, process, network, or credentials
Safe use on untrusted repositories requires external containerization or sandboxing
projects.why_it_matters: A compact open coding-agent harness that exposes reusable runtime components instead of prescribing a large platform.

projects.name: Prime Agent
projects.description: Long-running coding and research harness built around persistent IPython, recursive subagents, durable state, and bounded autonomy.
projects.canonical_data: daemon-backed sessions, persistent IPython state, goals, memories, skills, and versioned harness refinements
strengths: Persistent Python control environment makes tools and context programmable
Recursive subagents, background sessions, schedules, goals, and heartbeats support long work
Harness refinements are bounded, evidence-backed, versioned, and reversible
weaknesses: Generated Python and commands run with the user's permissions rather than a security sandbox
Persistent and self-editing state demand careful inspection and trust boundaries
The project is new despite rapid adoption
projects.why_it_matters: A distinctive open harness for durable, recursively delegated agent work where lifecycle and recovery are first-class.

projects.name: Pydantic AI
projects.description: Typed Python framework for production agent applications, tools, graphs, and evaluation.
projects.canonical_data: typed application-defined state
strengths: Typed contracts and validation
Strong observability and evaluation story
Broad provider and protocol support
weaknesses: Python-focused
Runtime policy remains application-defined
projects.why_it_matters: Shows how software-engineering rigor can reduce agent uncertainty.

projects.name: smolagents
projects.description: Compact agent library centered on code agents, tool calling, and model portability.
projects.canonical_data: application-defined state
strengths: Small understandable abstraction
Model portability
Supports local and sandboxed execution
weaknesses: Fewer durable-runtime primitives
Safety and persistence are largely application responsibilities
projects.why_it_matters: A useful counterpoint to heavier orchestration frameworks.

projects.name: Vanna
projects.description: User-aware SQL agent framework with executable database tools, permission-aware identity, tool memory, streaming UI components, and customizable lifecycle hooks.
projects.canonical_data: database schemas, tool-use memories, conversation state, permissions, and application-defined context
projects.current_repo_note: GitHub marks the repository archived; the reviewed Vanna 2.0 code and documentation remain available.
strengths: Executes and verifies SQL through explicit tools instead of returning text-only query suggestions
Propagates user identity and access groups through prompts, tools, and SQL filtering
Tool memory, custom tools, lifecycle hooks, and multiple model/database integrations are first-class
weaknesses: The public repository is archived, making its maintenance and successor path uncertain
Production safety depends on application-defined authentication, permissions, and database runner policy
The 2.0 rewrite increases migration cost for applications built on the older retrieval API
projects.why_it_matters: Demonstrates how a text-to-SQL agent can combine execution, learned examples, identity-aware permissions, and a production-facing interface.

projects.name: WrenAI
projects.description: Open-core generative-BI and text-to-SQL system with a governed semantic layer, validation tools, agent SDKs, MCP, and commercial agentic applications.
projects.canonical_data: Git-friendly MDL, instructions, query examples, and optional local semantic memory
projects.current_repo_note: The current open-core product separates its Apache-licensed engine and SDKs from commercial Agentic Mode, GenBI UI, security, and enterprise deployment features.
strengths: Semantic modeling, dry-plan validation, row limits, and structured errors make query correctness explicit
Apache-licensed CLI, MCP server, agent SDKs, and connectors support local and framework-driven workflows
Business definitions, query examples, and context remain human-reviewable and Git-friendly
weaknesses: The autonomous Agentic Mode, GenBI UI, access controls, and advanced deployment features are commercial
The open SDKs rely on an external agent framework or client to own the reasoning loop
Operating a governed semantic layer adds modeling and maintenance work before analysis
projects.why_it_matters: A strong example of data-agent reliability built from governed context, validation, recoverable errors, and explicit open-core boundaries.

projects.name: Claude Cowork
projects.description: Anthropic's delegated-work agent for completing multi-step knowledge work in an isolated cloud environment with files, connected tools, and persistent sessions.

Isolated cloud execution and explicit tool permissions create a clearer operational boundary
Persistent files and sessions support long-running knowledge-work projects across devices
weaknesses: Proprietary provider-native service with no self-hosted execution path
Available tools, limits, and retention controls vary by plan and continue to evolve
Remote execution and connected data require careful review of permissions and generated actions
projects.why_it_matters: Establishes delegated general knowledge work as a product boundary distinct from both conversational Claude and developer-facing Claude Code.

projects.name: Perplexity Computer
projects.description: Perplexity's independent digital worker for delegated research, connected-app workflows, artifact creation, communications, and scheduled work.

strengths: Broad delegated-work surface spanning research, communications, applications, files, and scheduling
Large connector catalog lets one task coordinate information and actions across services
Always-on and scheduled work extends beyond a synchronous research assistant
weaknesses: Proprietary managed execution with limited implementation and recovery inspectability
Connector breadth increases the permission, data-boundary, and consequential-action surface
New product whose controls, limits, and long-term operating model are still maturing
projects.why_it_matters: A prominent general work agent that combines Perplexity's research foundation with cross-application execution and asynchronous delegation.

projects.name: Amazon Quick
projects.description: AWS work assistant combining organizational knowledge, research, analytics, actions, custom agents, skills, and scheduled workflows.

strengths: Combines enterprise search, cited research, analytics, applications, and actions in one governed workspace
Custom agents, scheduled work, MCP and OpenAPI connections, and human-in-the-loop automation cover broad work patterns
Permission-aware organizational data and AWS administration provide a strong enterprise control boundary
weaknesses: Proprietary managed service with limited implementation inspectability
The broad product bundle and evolving desktop preview make capability boundaries and maturity uneven
Organizational context and long-term personalization are service-managed rather than local-first
projects.why_it_matters: A major hyperscaler reference for an enterprise assistant that unifies knowledge, agent creation, business actions, analytics, and persistent work context.

projects.name: ChatGPT
projects.description: OpenAI's general-purpose assistant for conversation, files, research, connected applications, memory, projects, and tool-using work.
projects.canonical_data: service-managed conversations, saved memory, projects, connected-app context, tasks, and generated work artifacts
projects.current_repo_note: This record covers the end-user ChatGPT product; Codex and OpenAI Agents SDK remain distinct operational systems.
strengths: Broad, mature assistant experience spanning research, files, creation, connected applications, and tool-using work
Projects, saved memory, recurring tasks, and cross-device clients support continuity across sessions
Strong usability, documentation, and ecosystem adoption
weaknesses: Operational implementation and model runtime are proprietary and provider-native
Capabilities, limits, retention controls, and available tools vary by plan and change frequently
Service-managed context and memory reduce data portability and local control
projects.why_it_matters: A reference general assistant whose product boundary now includes durable context, connected data, research, scheduled work, and consequential tool use—not only text chat.

projects.name: Claude
projects.description: Anthropic's consumer assistant for conversation, projects, files, research, connected applications, artifacts, and cross-chat memory.
projects.canonical_data: service-managed conversations, editable memory entries, project knowledge, connected-app context, files, and artifacts
projects.current_repo_note: This record covers the Claude Free, Pro, and Max end-user product; Claude for Work, Claude Code, and Claude Agent SDK have distinct operational and contractual boundaries.
strengths: Projects, project knowledge, cross-chat search, and editable memory provide strong continuity with visible user controls
Research combines iterative web and connected-app retrieval with citations and explicit steering
Files, artifacts, connected applications, and memory import/export support broad knowledge-work workflows
weaknesses: The operational implementation and model runtime are proprietary and provider-native
Memory, research, integrations, and usage limits vary by plan and rollout stage
Service-managed context and project knowledge are not local-first despite export and deletion controls
projects.why_it_matters: A leading general assistant reference for explicit projects, inspectable memory controls, connected research, and portable user context within a polished conversational workspace.

projects.name: DeepSeek

projects.current_repo_note: This record covers the end-user Venice assistant. The separately reviewed Venice API record covers the developer inference and routing service.
strengths: Presents a large cross-provider and cross-modal model catalog in one assistant workspace
Device-held history and clearly labeled private, anonymized, TEE, and E2EE model modes expose meaningful privacy choices
Search, files, generation, and model switching cover a broad interactive assistant workflow
weaknesses: Privacy properties differ materially by model mode and upstream frontier-provider routing
A proprietary service still mediates authentication, routing, billing, and most inference
Assistant tools remain less autonomous and recoverable than a general delegated-work agent
projects.why_it_matters: A useful comparison point for multi-model assistants that make routing privacy and local conversation history part of the product proposition.

projects.name: Weaviate
projects.description: Vector database with hybrid search and structured filtering.
projects.canonical_data: database
strengths: Strong reusable retrieval foundation
Broad ecosystem integrations
weaknesses: Not a second brain by itself
Requires ingestion, governance, provenance, and UX layers
projects.why_it_matters: Included as a building block so vector storage is visible without being mistaken for a product category.

projects.name: AdalFlow
projects.description: Library for building and automatically optimizing language-model workflows, combining a ReAct agent runtime with tool and MCP integration, retrieval components, tracing, and parameter-based prompt optimization.
projects.canonical_data: Python components, typed data classes, prompt parameters, tool definitions, retriever indexes, optimization traces, and run traces
strengths: Ships a ReAct agent runtime with function and MCP tool integration alongside retrieval components, so agent building is a first-class outcome rather than an add-on
Treats prompts as optimizable parameters, giving evaluation-driven tuning a place in the same programming model as the agent loop
Includes human-in-the-loop and tracing infrastructure without requiring an external service or additional API
weaknesses: Positioned as a general language-model workflow library, so agent execution shares attention with optimization concerns rather than dominating the design
Deployment, persistence, permissions, and production recovery remain application-defined
Repository activity is slower than the largest agent frameworks, and the operational track record behind the AdaL product is not independently documented
projects.why_it_matters: Represents the auto-optimization approach to agent construction, where prompts and demonstrations are tuned against metrics instead of hand-written, and is the open library beneath SylphAI's commercial AdaL coding agent.

projects.name: Strands Agents SDK
projects.description: Model-driven agent SDK from AWS that builds tool-using agents from a model, a prompt, and typed tools, with multi-provider model support, MCP integration, and multi-agent patterns.
projects.canonical_data: Agent definitions, typed tool implementations, prompts, session state, and MCP server configuration
projects.current_repo_note: AWS renamed the canonical repository from strands-agents/sdk-python to strands-agents/harness-sdk; the published packages remain strands-agents.
strengths: Model-driven design keeps agent definitions short while leaving tools, prompts, and model choice explicit
Publishes Python and TypeScript packages plus its own MCP server, so the same agent definition reaches several runtimes
Backed by AWS with documented multi-agent patterns and a separate maintained tools repository
weaknesses: The canonical repository was renamed, so older integration guides and third-party references point at a stale path
Persistence, permissions, and production recovery remain application-defined rather than framework-guaranteed
A large open-issue count relative to the project's age indicates a fast-moving surface
projects.why_it_matters: Gives the Atlas a provider-published, model-driven agent SDK whose design deliberately minimizes framework scaffolding, contrasting with graph-and-workflow frameworks.

projects.name: Genkit
projects.description: Open-source framework from Google's Firebase for building AI-powered application flows, with a unified model interface, tool calling, structured output, retrieval, evaluation, and a local developer UI.
projects.canonical_data: Flow definitions, typed schemas, prompt files, tool definitions, plugin configuration, retriever indexes, and evaluation runs
strengths: A local developer UI for running, inspecting, and evaluating flows makes agent behaviour observable during development rather than only in production
One model interface spans Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama backends through a documented plugin system
Built and used in production by Google's Firebase, with production-ready JavaScript and Go SDKs
weaknesses: Language support is uneven: Python is beta and Dart is preview, so cross-language parity cannot be assumed
The design centres on application flows, so long-running autonomous agent execution is less developed than in agent-first runtimes
Deployment guidance leans toward Google's hosting even though the framework itself is portable
projects.why_it_matters: Represents the application-framework approach to agent construction, where typed flows, evaluation, and a developer inspection loop matter more than autonomous execution.

projects.name: Mistral Vibe
projects.description: Mistral's end-user chat assistant for work and code, covering web search, document and spreadsheet analysis, document creation, workflow automation, repository-connected coding, and broad tool connectivity.
projects.canonical_data: service-managed conversations, settings, connected-tool context, generated documents, and code changes in connected repositories
projects.current_repo_note: Mistral renamed Le Chat to Vibe and states that conversations, settings, and plans carry over. This record covers the end-user assistant; Mistral AI Studio and the Mistral API remain distinct boundaries.
strengths: A French-incorporated provider under EU consumer terms gives European buyers a governance and jurisdiction boundary distinct from the US-operated assistants already in the catalogue
Enterprise plans document on-premises, private-cloud, and Mistral Cloud deployment with data residency, which is unusual for an end-user assistant product
Documents full MCP compatibility alongside repository integrations for GitHub, GitLab, and Jira, so the assistant reaches existing developer workflows
weaknesses: Training on user data is governed by an opt-out rather than an opt-in, so the default posture requires an explicit user action to change
The product was renamed from Le Chat to Vibe, so documentation, third-party guides, and support material are inconsistent about the product name
Durable project and memory behaviour is less clearly documented than in the longest-established assistants, which limits confidence in context continuity
projects.why_it_matters: Adds a European-governed general assistant whose enterprise path includes self-hosted and residency-bound deployment, a materially different governance boundary from the US provider assistants that dominate the family.

projects.name: AutoGen
projects.description: Layered Python and .NET framework for event-driven multi-agent applications, combining a message-passing core runtime, the AgentChat conversation API, model, tool, MCP, and code-executor extensions, and the AutoGen Studio prototyping GUI.
projects.canonical_data: Python and .NET agent and team definitions, declarative component configuration, message and event streams, serialized team state, and optional Chroma, Redis, or Mem0 memory stores
projects.current_repo_note: The README (fetched 2026-08-29) carries a maintenance-mode caution: AutoGen "is now in maintenance mode. It will not receive new features or enhancements and is community managed going forward." It directs new users to Microsoft Agent Framework as the "enterprise-ready successor to AutoGen," links an AutoGen to Microsoft Agent Framework migration guide, and limits contributions to bug fixes, security patches, and documentation. The repository's last push was 2026-04-15.
strengths: A layered design separates the event-driven Core API, the opinionated AgentChat API, and an Extensions package, so teams can work at the abstraction their problem needs rather than one fixed agent loop

Real execution surfaces ship in the repository: local, Jupyter, Docker, Docker-Jupyter, and Azure code executors, an MCP workbench for external tool servers, and AgentTool for exposing agents to other agents as delegated tools

Cross-language Python and .NET runtimes, published PyPI and NuGet packages, AutoGen Studio for no-code prototyping, and the AGBench evaluation suite gave the multi-agent patterns an unusually complete tooling story
weaknesses: Microsoft has declared it superseded: the README places AutoGen in maintenance mode, states it is community managed and will receive no new features, and tells new projects to start with Microsoft Agent Framework instead

Contributions are restricted to bug fixes, security patches, and documentation, and the last push was 2026-04-15, so model-client, protocol, and tool integrations will drift out of date faster than the framework can absorb
AutoGen Studio is explicitly labelled not production-ready, leaving authentication, security, and deployment concerns to the application developer
Users have already absorbed one breaking migration from v0.2 to v0.4, and the move to Microsoft Agent Framework asks them to absorb a second
projects.why_it_matters: AutoGen took conversational multi-agent orchestration out of Microsoft Research and into mainstream practice, and Microsoft names it the direct predecessor of Microsoft Agent Framework; recording it as superseded keeps that lineage legible instead of leaving a heavily adopted framework looking like a current recommendation.

projects.name: Semantic Kernel
projects.description: Model-agnostic Python, .NET, and Java SDK for building agents and multi-agent systems from kernels, plugins and kernel functions, prompt templates, filters, OpenAPI and MCP connectors, vector-store integrations, and the Process Framework.
projects.canonical_data: Kernel configurations, plugins and kernel functions, prompt templates, agent definitions, chat-history threads, process definitions, and records in connected vector stores
projects.current_repo_note: The README (fetched 2026-08-29) opens with an important notice: "Semantic Kernel is now Microsoft Agent Framework!" It describes Microsoft Agent Framework as "the enterprise-ready successor to Semantic Kernel," now at a production-ready 1.0 with stable APIs and long-term support, and points readers to a Semantic Kernel migration guide. Unlike AutoGen, the README carries no maintenance-mode notice and the repository still received commits on 2026-08-27.
strengths: Genuinely multi-language rather than a Python project with ports: maintained Python, .NET, and Java trees in one repository with published PyPI and NuGet packages and per-language API references

A wide substitutable integration surface — OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Hugging Face, and NVIDIA NIM backends plus documented local execution through Ollama, LM Studio, and ONNX, alongside Azure AI Search, Chroma, Elasticsearch, Qdrant, Postgres, Redis, Pinecone, MongoDB, Weaviate, and FAISS connectors

Explicit developer control surfaces: typed kernel functions, OpenAPI and MCP plugins, function-choice behavior, filters, reliability policies, structured output through Pydantic models, and the Process Framework for modeling business workflows
weaknesses: Microsoft has declared it superseded: the README's first line states Semantic Kernel "is now Microsoft Agent Framework" and names that project the enterprise-ready successor, so new work is steered away from this SDK even though commits continue

The successor announcement is not paired with a stated support horizon in the repository, so adopters cannot tell from authoritative repository sources how long Semantic Kernel will keep receiving fixes
Feature parity differs by language, which is why the project maintains a separate supported-languages feature matrix; a capability demonstrated in the Python samples is not guaranteed in .NET or Java
Quickstarts, samples, and defaults are Azure-first, so the model-agnostic design takes more work to realize outside the Azure OpenAI path
projects.why_it_matters: Semantic Kernel is the enterprise-facing half of the lineage that Microsoft consolidated into Microsoft Agent Framework, and it is the framework that carried plugin-based agent orchestration into .NET and Java shops; recording it as superseded preserves that reach while pointing adopters at the maintained path.

projects.name: Meta AI
projects.description: Meta's consumer AI assistant for conversation, research, files and media, voice, image generation, scheduled tasks, and shopping across Meta's apps, the web, desktop, and AI glasses.
projects.canonical_data: service-managed conversations, saved personalization memory, uploaded photos, files and documents, and generated media held under Meta's AI terms and privacy policy
projects.current_repo_note: This record covers the consumer Meta AI assistant as one governed product across meta.ai, the iOS, Android and Mac clients, AI glasses, and the Facebook, Messenger, Instagram and WhatsApp surfaces; Meta Model API and Muse Code are separate operational records.
strengths: One assistant product spans text, voice, camera and live vision, file and document analysis, deep research, image generation, and scheduled tasks
Unusually broad access: free clients for iOS, Android, web and Mac plus AI glasses and the Facebook, Messenger, Instagram and WhatsApp surfaces
Incognito chats run under Private Processing, which Meta documents as inaccessible to Meta, and personalization memory is user-managed
weaknesses: Governing AI terms allow interactions to personalize experiences and ads and to be reviewed by automated or human systems, and warn that deleting messages, threads, or an account may not delete Meta's copy
No model choice beyond Instant and Thinking modes, no public assistant API, and no documented conversation export or open connector surface
Capabilities, voice languages, and applicable terms vary by region, and the Mac client is still beta
Product boundary churns quickly: AI Studio character creation was retired in August 2026 and the assistant was moved onto Muse Spark
projects.why_it_matters: The highest-distribution consumer assistant boundary, and a reference case for how a general assistant behaves when its terms tie personal interactions to advertising personalization rather than to a tenant data boundary.

projects.name: Muse Code
projects.description: Meta's proprietary terminal coding agent for Muse Spark, with OS-enforced sandboxing, staged shell approval, parallel subagents in isolated git worktrees, skills, hooks, and MCP.
projects.canonical_data: the local working tree, per-subagent git worktrees, project-local skills, rules and hooks under .agents, and resumable Muse Code session logs and run journals
projects.current_repo_note: Muse Code ships as a proprietary native binary installed from dev.meta.ai with no public source repository; it is billed either through a Muse Code subscription or pay-as-you-go on a Meta Model API key, which remains a separate service record.
strengths: Approval and an OS-enforced sandbox (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux) are on by default, and compound shell commands are reviewed stage by stage rather than as one line
Trust is granted at explicit scopes with workspace-rooted prefix rules, deny precedence, and a refusal to save interpreter prefixes as broad allows
Parallel subagents can be isolated in per-child git worktrees so the lead's working copy is untouched, with journaled spawns, status changes, and control actions
Extensible through skills, hooks, and MCP, and it imports skills from other agents' repo-local .claude and .codex directories
weaknesses: Beta at version 0.2.x with terms that cover a limited preview period; there is no public repository or issue tracker and no Windows build
Provider-native to Meta Model API, so model processing is remote and the harness cannot be pointed at a self-hosted backend
Subagent cancellation is cooperative, so a child that never reaches a checkpoint keeps running
Background observer agents make their own model calls and add token usage on top of the main session
projects.why_it_matters: Meta's entry into provider-native coding agents, and a notably explicit reference for staged shell approval, workspace trust scoping, and worktree-isolated parallel subagents.

projects.name: Microsoft Foundry Agent Service
projects.description: Managed Azure service that runs configured or containerized agents with hosted tools, per-session sandboxes, persistent conversations, and directory identities.
projects.canonical_data: agent versions, conversation threads, run state, uploaded files, vector stores, per-session sandbox filesystems, and memory stores
strengths: Standard setup keeps files, vector stores, threads, and agent definitions in the customer's own Azure Storage, AI Search, and Cosmos DB resources
Each hosted agent receives a dedicated Microsoft Entra identity and a per-session isolated sandbox with a persistent filesystem
Toolboxes expose curated tools through one managed protocol endpoint that non-Foundry runtimes can consume unchanged
weaknesses: Agent-side quotas are fixed and documented as unable to be increased, including 128 tools per agent, 100,000 messages per thread, and 1,000 agent revisions
Memory, skills, tool search, agent-to-agent endpoints, and long-running resilience remain in preview, and the resilience documentation is not recommended for production
Tool availability varies by region and model rather than being uniform across the service
projects.why_it_matters: A vendor-operated runtime that enterprises use to host agents written in other frameworks, so its identity, storage, and approval boundaries become those agents' operating envelope.

projects.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
projects.description: Managed AWS platform that hosts, secures, and observes agents built in any framework, with memory, tool gateways, and policy enforcement.
projects.canonical_data: agent session state, persistent session filesystems, and extracted long-term memory records
strengths: Runtime hosts CrewAI, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Google ADK, OpenAI Agents SDK, and Strands agents, or no framework at all
Every session runs in a dedicated micro virtual machine that is terminated and sanitized when the session ends
Policy intercepts each tool call at the gateway against declarative rules before execution and logs every decision
weaknesses: The tool allowlist is not a containment boundary: it does not constrain the direct command-invocation API, so containment depends entirely on account permissions
Customer-managed encryption keys cover only memory and gateway resources, and gateway names, target names, tool names, and gateway logs are documented as unencrypted by default
The low-code harness path cannot use a framework of the customer's choice, and its export escape hatch produces one vendor's framework in one language
projects.why_it_matters: The operated substrate beneath agents built in other frameworks, selling hosting, memory, tool governance, and tracing as a service rather than a library.

projects.name: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
projects.description: Google Cloud's managed runtime for agents built in its own and third-party frameworks, with hosted sessions, long-term memory, and a governing gateway.
projects.canonical_data: deployed agent revisions, session event histories, and generated long-term memories
strengths: Hosts agents written in the vendor's own kit plus LangChain, LangGraph, AG2, LlamaIndex, and CrewAI, or any container meeting a published runtime contract
Memory Bank provides consolidation, immutable revision history, per-identity scoping, and customer-set expiry rather than a bare vector store
Agent Registry gives one catalog for storing, discovering, and governing agents, tool servers, and endpoints across an organization
weaknesses: The gateway that enforces policy does not support the platform's own network perimeter controls, by its own documented limitation
Long-term memories never expire unless an expiry is set, and no retention period is documented for traces or logs
No retry, backoff, or failure-recovery semantics are documented, and the only rollback mechanism remains in preview
Pause-and-approve exists only by inheriting one framework's breakpoints; no framework-neutral human-approval interface is documented
projects.why_it_matters: A major cloud vendor's managed runtime for other people's agent frameworks, and a reference point for how hosted agent state, identity, and governance are productized.

projects.name: IBM watsonx Orchestrate
projects.description: Enterprise platform that registers and routes between agents from other vendors over open protocols, with hosted, on-premises, and air-gapped deployments.
projects.canonical_data: agent, tool, and knowledge-base definitions with conversation threads and execution traces
strengths: Registers external agents by typed provider across six integrations, including another vendor's customer-relationship agents and a competitor's low-code agents
Documented air-gapped on-premises operation with a release-by-release compatibility matrix and a local package-registry procedure
Model-neutral through a gateway spanning fourteen providers, including self-hosted options
weaknesses: The open component is the client: the runtime that plans, routes, and selects collaborators is proprietary, so routing behavior can be observed through vendor traces but never read
The vendor's own known-issues list documents tools running before required inputs arrive, repeated identical tool calls, and failed agent-to-agent transfers
The local Developer Edition is licensed to a single developer, cannot deploy, and still routes inputs and outputs through the vendor's cloud
projects.why_it_matters: One of the few systems that puts agents from several vendors behind one registry, one policy layer, and one trace log, including on hardware the customer owns.

projects.current_repo_note: GitHub reports NOASSERTION, which is correct here: the licence is a modified Apache 2.0 rather than the standard text, so no identifier applies.
projects.name: Dify
projects.description: Platform for building LLM applications, agents, and workflows on a visual canvas, self-hosted or vendor-hosted.
projects.canonical_data: application definitions as versioned YAML, knowledge-base documents and embeddings, and conversation and workflow run logs
strengths: A human-input node makes approval and review a first-class workflow step, deliverable by email to people without an account
Applications export and import as versioned declarative files, so the definition itself is portable
Persistence is backend-agnostic across several relational databases and many vector stores
weaknesses: The licence is a modified Apache 2.0 that forbids operating a multi-tenant environment and forbids removing frontend branding, so it is source-available rather than open source
Its own documentation states the agent runtime is not intended as a hardened security boundary between mutually untrusted users
The hosted terms of service carry no version or last-updated date, so changes cannot be tracked
projects.why_it_matters: A visual application builder that has grown an autonomous agent runtime, testing whether canvas tools and coding agents converge.

projects.name: Langflow
projects.description: Python platform for building agent and retrieval workflows on a visual canvas, then running exported flows anywhere.
projects.canonical_data: flow definitions as JSON graphs, plus chat message history and run logs
strengths: Plain MIT with no carve-outs and no separately licensed enterprise directory, the least encumbered option among comparable builders
A separate executor package runs exported flows statelessly with no database and no interface, decoupling the runtime from the builder
Flows version as normalized JSON with command-line validate, push, pull, and export, giving canvas work a real delivery path
weaknesses: No human approval or pause-for-review primitive is documented, unlike comparable builders
One structured output mode silently skips playground events and chat-history writes, creating an observability gap
Marketing advertises a free cloud account that no retrievable first-party service page or documentation supports
projects.why_it_matters: The permissively licensed canvas whose flows run as portable JSON outside the builder, making visual authoring compatible with code-based deployment.

projects.current_repo_note: The public botpress/botpress repository holds integrations, the command-line tool, and SDKs under MIT; the studio, engine, and runtime are closed and hosted, and the discontinued self-hosted product lives in a separate repository under AGPL-3.0.
projects.name: Botpress Cloud
projects.description: Vendor-hosted platform for building and running customer-support agents, with a visual studio, a typed SDK, and human handoff.
projects.canonical_data: bot definitions, structured tables, knowledge-base sources, and conversation history
strengths: Human handoff is a first-class product surface rather than a feature, with a dedicated escalation agent, a console for human operators, and handoff interfaces in the SDK
A genuine code-first authoring path exists alongside the canvas, with typed primitives discovered from the filesystem and automated conversation tests
Conversation-metered pricing with unlimited seats on paid tiers, under dated published terms
weaknesses: No self-hosting, on-premises, or data-residency option is documented anywhere, so the vendor holds all data unconditionally
Bot export is a proprietary archive users are told not to open, which excludes knowledge-base files and fails above roughly three gigabytes
What the product calls agents are components running in a fixed order around one bot rather than peers that hand off to each other
projects.why_it_matters: A visual bot builder narrowed into a hosted support product, where the durable differentiator is human escalation rather than agent autonomy.

projects.current_repo_note: GitHub reports NOASSERTION; the repository actually splits Apache-2.0 for the bulk against a commercial licence covering packages/server/src/enterprise. Archived on 2026-08-13 with end of life announced for 2026-08-31 and no successor named.
projects.name: Flowise
projects.description: Visual builder for agent and retrieval workflows, wound down by its maintainers with development frozen and the repository archived.
projects.canonical_data: flow definitions, chat history, and document stores
strengths: The bulk of the code is Apache-2.0 and the maintainers explicitly encourage forking it after the wind-down
A large adoption base and fork count leave substantial community material behind the archived repository
Both licences are stated in-repository with an explicit directory-level carve-out rather than left to detection
weaknesses: Development ceased on 2026-07-29 and the repository was archived on 2026-08-13, with published packages and images deprecated
No successor or endorsed fork is named, so a reader gets no migration target from the maintainers
The enterprise directory stays under a commercial licence conditioned on a subscription from a company winding the product down, and the fate of the hosted service is undocumented
projects.why_it_matters: A widely adopted visual builder whose maintainers wound it down citing the shift to coding agents, making it a dated reference point for that transition.

projects.name: Microsoft Copilot Studio
projects.description: Vendor-operated low-code service for configuring agents that use connectors and knowledge, coordinate child agents, and escalate to people.
projects.canonical_data: agent definitions, knowledge sources, tool configurations, and conversation transcripts retained for a bounded period
strengths: Human escalation is a first-class construct with a dedicated transfer step, a documented context contract for routing, and escalation marked in analytics
Coordinates child agents, other tenants' agents over an open protocol, and agents from three sibling Microsoft products
Knowledge sources resolve under the signed-in user's identity, so an agent surfaces only content that user may already see
weaknesses: The runtime is vendor-operated with no self-hosted option, and agent definitions live in the vendor's own data platform
Capability is bounded by the surrounding ecosystem, and the richest connectors, channels, and knowledge sources are first-party
Conversation transcripts are retained only for a bounded window before automatic deletion, limiting long-range audit
projects.why_it_matters: The low-code path into a major vendor's agent ecosystem, and the clearest case that a visual builder can be an orchestrator rather than a framework.

projects.current_repo_note: Salesforce groups this platform under Einstein Platform in its trust documentation, alongside prebuilt Agentforce assistants and legacy Einstein features. Agentforce Vibes, Contact Center, IT Service, Operations, and Supply Chain are documented separately and are outside this record.
projects.name: Salesforce Agentforce
projects.description: Vendor-operated platform for configuring agents as declarative org metadata that serve a customer's own customers or employees.
projects.canonical_data: agent and version metadata, subagent and action definitions, indexed knowledge libraries, and server-side conversation sessions
strengths: Agents are declarative metadata that deploy, version, and promote through the vendor's ordinary release tooling rather than living only in a console
Human escalation is a first-class construct with a dedicated subagent and a routing path into the vendor's contact-centre queueing
Actions reuse existing org logic directly, so database queries, business flows, and custom code become agent capabilities without a separate integration layer
weaknesses: The runtime is vendor-operated inside a customer org with no self-hosted option, so execution and data both stay on the vendor's infrastructure
Capability is bounded by the surrounding platform: the richest actions, knowledge sources, and escalation targets are all first-party
The brand covers prebuilt assistants and several separately sold products, so published material about “Agentforce” often describes something other than this platform
projects.why_it_matters: The agent-building layer inside one of the largest enterprise data platforms, where the agent's reach is defined by records and permissions the organisation already maintains.

projects.current_repo_note: Meta Business AI is a marketing umbrella covering advertising automation and creative tooling; this record covers only the separately documented agent platform and its own terms.
projects.name: Meta Business Agent Platform
projects.description: Vendor-operated platform where a business configures a messaging agent through APIs, grounding it in its own content and connecting its own systems.
projects.canonical_data: agent configuration, business knowledge sources, skill definitions, and connected action endpoints
strengths: Handoff between the agent and the business's own application is a documented first-class capability rather than an escalation afterthought
The agent takes real actions through the business's own interfaces and webhook subscriptions rather than only retrieving answers
A test surface for sending messages and evaluating behaviour is documented before and after going live
weaknesses: The platform serves one messaging channel on eligible business phone numbers, so it is not a general agent surface
Eligibility excludes several regulated categories outright, including finance, government, health, alcohol, gambling, and over-the-counter drugs
The published documentation surface is small, and the governing terms render only in a browser, so their text could not be re-read during this review
projects.why_it_matters: Shows a messaging platform turning its business channel into a configurable agent surface, where reach is defined by the channel rather than by the customer's own systems.

projects.current_repo_note: Distributed for one host command line under the separate name LazyCodex, whose repository is a thin installer that vendors this engine as a submodule; the installer carries a permissive licence but the engine it fetches does not.
projects.name: oh-my-openagent
projects.description: A plugin adding multi-agent orchestration, planning, and code-navigation tooling to an existing coding command line, plus a standalone edition.
projects.canonical_data: project and user configuration, hierarchical instruction files, and stored plans
strengths: Runs inside command lines developers already use rather than requiring them to adopt a new agent
Hash-anchored editing gives the model a verifiable line identifier, addressing a documented class of edit failure
Existing hooks, commands, skills, and tool servers from another vendor's agent are explicitly supported unchanged
weaknesses: The licence permits only internal, personal, or non-commercial use and forbids paid redistribution, so it is source-available rather than open source
Every current release is a prerelease of a major version, against roughly nine hundred open issues and a structural refactor in progress
Package, binary, and configuration names are mid-rename, and an unrelated package occupies the short name on the public registry
projects.why_it_matters: The most-adopted attempt to let a third-party plugin, rather than a vendor, define the orchestration layer above whichever coding command line a developer already runs.

projects.name: Gajae-Code
projects.description: A terminal coding agent that authenticates against existing subscriptions, gates edits behind an approved plan, and relays questions to chat apps.
projects.canonical_data: append-only session logs with content-addressed blobs, plus consolidated memory files and generated playbooks
strengths: Authenticates against subscriptions the developer already pays for across many providers, avoiding a second metered bill
Mutation is gated behind an approved plan, and the project ships no permission-bypass flag by design
Unattended runs are bounded by a lease that only real tool execution renews, so streaming text cannot keep a stalled run alive
weaknesses: The project declares itself experimental and pre-release and tells users to verify outputs before relying on them
Retrieval is keyword, structural, and language-server based, with no semantic or vector search documented
Automatic memory is disabled by default and its artifacts are private runtime state rather than a supported interface
projects.why_it_matters: The clearest worked example of a coding agent designed around subscription authentication and asynchronous human approval rather than metered billing and terminal presence.

projects.current_repo_note: The repository describes itself as maintained without human intervention; its philosophy document instead describes humans directing work through a chat channel while agents implement, its contributor guide is conventional, and recent commits carry a dozen human author identities with no automated account. Direct pushes to the main branch are policy-blocked and merges are performed by people.
projects.name: Claw Code
projects.description: A command-line coding agent written in Rust and modelled on an existing vendor agent, published as a demonstration rather than a supported tool.
projects.canonical_data: in-workspace session files, worker state, and layered instruction files
strengths: Permissions are explicit and safe by default, with full access requiring a deliberate opt-in and a pre-dispatch enforcement gate
Every diagnostic command emits structured output, including build provenance and per-entry validation errors for tool servers and hooks
Runs against local compatible model servers, so it need not call a hosted interface at all
weaknesses: Its own maintainers state it is not the serious production project and direct users to two other tools to do real work
There are no releases and no tags at all, installation is build-from-source only, and the same-named package on the language registry installs a deprecated stub
The claim that it is maintained without human intervention is contradicted by its own contributor guide and by a commit history with a dozen human authors and no automated account
projects.why_it_matters: A highly visible demonstration that agent-executed development can sustain a large codebase, and an equally clear illustration of the distance between that and a shippable tool.

projects.current_repo_note: The project describes an open-core structure, but everything in the repository carries one permissive licence; the reserved capabilities are hosted-service features such as cloud sync, team memory, administration, and enterprise access control rather than restricted source, so the record classifies it by the code it publishes.
projects.name: claude-mem
projects.description: Captures coding-agent tool activity through lifecycle hooks, summarises it, and stores it locally for later retrieval.
projects.canonical_data: tool-use observations and session summaries, scoped per project
strengths: The only one of its peers exposing its store through a documented interface, a tool protocol, and an embeddable package at once
Provenance is a first-class table rather than a metadata blob
Cross-project leakage is blocked in the database itself rather than by application convention
weaknesses: Two storage models coexist and the newer one is documented as not yet read by any live path
Writing a memory requires a language model, so the default configuration sends session content off the device
The project's own readme closes with a promoted cryptocurrency token, which is unusual for infrastructure a team would adopt
projects.why_it_matters: The most widely installed memory layer for coding agents, and the only one of its peers reachable through an interface, a tool protocol, and a package simultaneously.

projects.name: agentmemory
projects.description: A local memory server for coding agents that captures tool use through hooks and serves it over a tool protocol and an interface.
projects.canonical_data: tool-use observations consolidated into memories, lessons, and graph entities
strengths: Runs entirely offline with no key and no model calls, using lexical search with optional on-device embeddings
Supersession, decay, expiry, and eviction are separate implemented modules rather than a single forget flag
Memory exports to a plain markdown vault and synchronises in both directions with a project memory file
weaknesses: A hard dependency on a pinned third-party engine version the project cannot yet run without
More open issues than closed ones on a project roughly six months old and still before its first stable release
Repository hygiene is uneven; the root design document describes an unrelated car manufacturer's website rather than this system
projects.why_it_matters: The fullest open implementation of memory lifecycle mechanics, including supersession, decay, and a temporal graph, and it runs without any model key.

projects.current_repo_note: The licence file follows the structure of a well-known permissive licence but rewrites its grant using the wording of a different one, so no standard identifier applies and the hosting platform reports it only as other. The project's package metadata has its licence declaration commented out and publishes with none.
projects.name: memU
projects.description: A memory store and companion process that mines agent session logs into markdown notes and reusable skills, retrieved by embedding.
projects.canonical_data: markdown memory notes and extracted reusable skills, held in two tracks
strengths: The core is small and inspectable, and the store itself makes no model calls at all
Memory lands on disk as plain markdown with front matter, editable by hand and readable if the tool is removed
One configured backend is shared across every host, so what one agent's sessions taught it, another retrieves
weaknesses: The licence file is a non-canonical rewrite that no identifier matches, and the package metadata declares no licence at all
No local embedding option is documented, so even the private deployment sends memory content to a third-party interface
Retrieval is cosine similarity alone, with no lexical fallback, reranking, recency, or temporal filtering
projects.why_it_matters: Shows how far a memory service gets by storing plain markdown and delegating every judgement to the calling agent, at the cost of any built-in memory reasoning.

projects.current_repo_note: The memory implementation lives in a separate component referenced as a submodule, which carries the same strong copyleft licence as the application.
projects.name: OpenHuman
projects.description: A desktop assistant that ingests connected accounts into a local markdown memory tree and runs agents over it.
projects.canonical_data: hierarchical markdown summary trees over connected accounts, plus a canonical entity registry
strengths: Memory is a folder of editable markdown the user owns, and the same files the agent reasons over are the ones a person can open and correct
A local-only mode is enforced where the inference client is constructed, so no code path can reach a hosted model while it is set
Change tracking maps onto real version-control primitives, so a reader can ask what changed since they last looked
weaknesses: It is an assistant rather than a memory service: no external interface, package, or tool protocol lets other software read its memory
A strong copyleft licence with a hosted subscription backend makes it hard to embed or to run wholly independently at default settings
The project labels itself early beta, and its memory core has only just been extracted into a separate component
projects.why_it_matters: The clearest working demonstration that a personal assistant's memory can be a plain markdown vault the owner reads and corrects by hand.

projects.name: LibreChat
projects.description: Self-hosted multi-user chat workspace that routes many model providers through one interface, with agents, MCP tools, and file handling.
projects.canonical_data: conversations, messages, agents, prompts, files, and per-user memory entries in an operator-run MongoDB
strengths: Routes Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure, Bedrock, Google, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint through one workspace
A hash-chained immutable audit log with ACL, role, and group permissions gives operators real multi-tenant governance
Re-exposes its own agents over chat-completions and Open Responses endpoints, so the workspace is also an addressable backend
weaknesses: Package manifests declare ISC while the license file and GitHub both report MIT
Memory entries are keyed upserts with no revision history, so an automatic write overwrites the prior value
File search needs MongoDB, Meilisearch, pgvector, and a separate retrieval API before it works
projects.why_it_matters: The most complete open self-hosted counterpart to hosted multi-model assistants, holding conversations, agents, and permissions in infrastructure the operator controls.

projects.name: DeerFlow
