weaknesses: Every first-party hosted surface the readme sends readers to is gone, including the homepage, the cloud sign-in, the playground, and the documented cloud host
Development has stopped, with no commit for eight months and no client release for longer, while the same organisation promotes a different project
Its capture surface is narrower than its client advertises: the library offers six content types but the server processes only two and rejects the rest
projects.why_it_matters: The clearest worked example of agent memory as a configurable, editable user profile plus an event timeline over an ordinary database, rather than a similarity search over accumulated facts.

projects.name: SeekrFlow
projects.description: Enterprise platform whose hosted agents run on durable threads with server-side tools, base or fine-tuned models, and response-level source attribution, deployable from Seekr's cloud to air-gapped sites.
projects.canonical_data: agent configurations and revisions, threads and messages, run spans, uploaded files, vector databases, and fine-tuned model artifacts
strengths: One platform spans document ingestion, fine-tuning, model deployment, and hosted agents, with the same records reachable from the web interface, a versioned REST API, and an Apache-2.0 Python SDK
Deployment reaches the customer's own cloud, on-premises hardware, and air-gapped edge sites under a published per-GPU annual licence, so completions need not leave the operator's environment

Explainability is a platform component rather than an add-on: context attribution, training-data attribution, and source tracing map a response back to retrieved chunks and to the training examples that shaped the model
Interoperates through an OpenAI-compatible client path, a LangChain integration, Vercel AI SDK streaming, a remote MCP connector, and an AWS Bedrock backend option for self-hosted clusters
weaknesses: The product page advertises agents that retain memory across sessions and adapt to user history, but the documentation index contains no memory surface at all; durable state is threads and messages only

Documented observability spans capture timing, model, token counts, and error type, which is narrower than the advertised record of every tool call and decision, and no replay or checkpoint recovery is documented
No human-approval gate, tool-call policy, or steering control is documented beyond cancelling an in-progress run

Commercial terms for the platform are not published: the terms the sign-up flow requires agreement to describe Seekr's consumer search application, and the Trust Center's legal documents sit behind an access request
projects.why_it_matters: A vendor-operated agent runtime aimed at operators who must keep inference and completions inside their own perimeter, and one that treats response-level attribution as a first-class platform surface rather than a tracing add-on.

projects.name: OzBrain
projects.description: Hosted shared knowledge base that AI agents and team members read and write through MCP and the web, with staged writes, provenance, and freshness tracking.
projects.canonical_data: a hosted store of versioned, provenance-tracked markdown articles behind OzBrain's own API and web app, shared by connected agents and human teammates
strengths: Staged writes with explicit promotion and role-based permissions (viewer/commenter/editor) prevent agents from silently overwriting a team's shared knowledge
Provenance and freshness are tracked per article, and the entire brain can be exported as plain markdown at any time
MCP-based connectors reach Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini, and other MCP-compatible clients without any local install
weaknesses: Single-founder, fully proprietary SaaS with no self-hosting option and no independent GitHub or adoption evidence to corroborate its claims
Retrieval is documented as keyword search over a routing index; no vector or semantic search is described
Data residency and compliance detail is thin: Supabase/Vercel hosting regions are only described as 'configured,' and no SOC 2 or similar certification is published
projects.why_it_matters: A small, clearly specified reference for a shared, human-and-agent-editable knowledge base with an explicit staging and promotion workflow, distinct from personal-only PKM tools and from silent auto-capture memory services.

projects.name: Nia
projects.description: Hosted indexing and retrieval API that gives coding and research agents one interface to search, traverse, and cite code, docs, datasets, and synced personal sources, with an open CLI client and optional self-hosting.
projects.canonical_data: a hosted index of code, docs, datasets, and other indexed sources behind Nia's proprietary API, plus files and synced personal data that stay on the user's own machine when configured that way
projects.current_repo_note: The nozomio-labs GitHub org hosts small open client repositories (nia-cli under Apache-2.0, plus a setup wizard, Claude Code plugin, and agent skill); the indexer, vector store, and ranking logic served from trynia.ai are closed and hosted, and self-hosted deployment of that stack is offered only as an enterprise arrangement.
strengths: Broad source coverage (code repos, documentation sites, PDFs, HuggingFace datasets, package manifests, local folders) served through one API, CLI, MCP server, and a Claude Code skill/plugin

Private repositories, files, and local folders are processed and kept on the user's machine, personal sync sources (iMessage, notes, browser history) use on-device zero-knowledge encryption, and the full indexing stack can be self-hosted

Publishes a methodology-documented hallucination/retrieval benchmark against GPT-5 and named competitors (Context7, Exa Code, Brave Search), backed by a YC-funded team shipping several open client repositories
weaknesses: The benchmark claiming the lowest error rate is self-administered by Nia against a judge model Nia also controls, with no independent reproduction found

Only thin client repositories (CLI, wizard, plugin, skill) are open; the indexer, vector store, and ranking logic that do the actual retrieval work are closed and disclosed only through the self-hosting enterprise offer
Indexed content is documented as needing periodic reindexing to stay current rather than being continuously and automatically refreshed
projects.why_it_matters: A YC-backed retrieval layer purpose-built to sit in front of coding and research agents, notable for pairing a genuinely open CLI/MCP client with documented data-sovereignty controls and a self-hosting option alongside its proprietary hosted API.

projects.name: Exo Harness
projects.description: Self-modifying agent harness that separates a durable, event-sourced substrate from swappable agent semantics, letting an agent safely evolve its own prompts, tools, and code.
projects.canonical_data: SQLite/Postgres-backed append-only conversation event log (UUIDv7-ordered) plus committed prompt/config files, artifacts, and sandbox snapshot references
strengths: A clean exoharness/executor split keeps durable state, sandbox lifecycle, and secrets in an immutable, event-sourced substrate while agent semantics (prompts, tools, compaction, model choice) stay fully swappable and self-editable
Named executor presets let a turn be delegated to Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or Pi running inside the managed sandbox, alongside first-class OpenAI, Anthropic, and OpenRouter model bindings
A durable append-only event log, live event streaming, and per-service logs give strong visibility into a self-modifying agent's history, with sandbox snapshot/rewind for backing out of bad changes
weaknesses: No GitHub releases or tags exist; the project ships directly off main at a fixed 0.1.0, and the README calls it early-stage, with self-maintenance, recoverable execution, and full clone/lineage-based multi-agent orchestration listed as unbuilt roadmap items

Recursive self-modification of harness policy, tools, and prompts is bounded only by an immutable event log as a policy choice; no documented human approval gate exists before the agent rebuilds and restarts its own runtime
Sandbox snapshot and rewind do not yet work across process restarts, and generalized computer-use of windowed GUIs is an acknowledged gap
projects.why_it_matters: One of the few open harnesses built explicitly around recursive self-modification: it isolates an immutable event log and sandbox substrate from fully agent-editable semantics, letting future models safely evolve every layer of their own runtime rather than only their memory.

projects.name: BabyAGI
projects.description: Archived reference implementation of the original 2023 task-driven autonomous agent loop: an LLM creates, prioritizes, and executes tasks toward an objective, storing each result in a local vector store to inform the next task.
projects.canonical_data: an in-memory task queue plus executed task results embedded and upserted into a local Chroma collection (or Weaviate/Pinecone) keyed by objective
projects.current_repo_note: The live yoheinakajima/babyagi repository (22k+ stars) now hosts an unrelated, actively developed 'functionz' function-registration framework under the same name and maintainer, not a continuation of this task-loop agent; that project is tracked separately in the candidate queue. This record covers yoheinakajima/babyagi_archive, the maintainer's own September 2024 snapshot of the original, which is not itself GitHub-flagged archived but receives no further commits and is presented in its own README as a historical snapshot.
strengths: Introduced the create-prioritize-execute-store loop that became the reference architecture for the 2023 wave of autonomous LLM agents; its own docs/inspired-projects.md lists the derivatives it spawned
Runs fully local-first when paired with Llama.cpp and the default local Chroma store, with no mandatory cloud dependency
A working Ray-backed cooperative mode lets multiple instances share one detached task queue and objective, a genuine (if partial) multi-instance extension
weaknesses: No approval step, budget cap, or stopping condition exists; task creation and prioritization run on unvalidated LLM text parsing, and continuous runs are documented as able to run up API costs indefinitely
The in-memory task queue is lost on any crash or restart; only vector-store results persist, so there is no real checkpoint or replay

The repository is a static September 2024 snapshot with no ongoing maintenance, and the live yoheinakajima/babyagi repository now reuses the same name for an unrelated project, which can mislead readers looking for the original
Distributed cooperative mode, as opposed to local, is an unimplemented stub in the shipped code
projects.why_it_matters: The original create-prioritize-execute task loop that seeded the 2023 wave of autonomous LLM agents (AutoGPT and its many forks); most later agent frameworks either extended this pattern or were built explicitly to fix its lack of tool use, approvals, and recovery.

projects.name: Dendron
projects.description: Editor-based note tool that organises Markdown notes in a strict hierarchy with schemas, lookup, refactoring, and a publishing pipeline.
projects.canonical_data: a vault of Markdown notes on disk, named by hierarchy, with schemas and configuration the user owns
projects.current_repo_note: Archived on the maintainer's own published declaration, not on a platform flag: the readme states active development has ceased and the project is in maintenance only, following a public announcement that the company behind it did not find a viable business. No successor is named, so the supersession status does not apply. The last commit touching product code is from August 2023, no releases exist, and the editor extension has not been updated since; its documentation site and published vaults still resolve. A search across its whole source tree finds no model or embedding code, so it is a plain note tool rather than an assisted one.
strengths: Hierarchical naming with schemas makes structure enforceable rather than conventional, so a large vault stays navigable by lookup instead of by memory
Notes are ordinary Markdown files on disk that survive the tool, and the publishing pipeline turns a vault into a site the author owns
Import and export adapters move whole vaults between other note tools without a proprietary intermediate format
weaknesses: Development ceased in early 2023 by the maintainer's own declaration, with no release since and hundreds of issues left open
It has no model or embedding code anywhere in its tree, so every assisted-retrieval capability its neighbours offer is absent
Licence metadata is inconsistent: several packages declare no licence at all, others use a non-standard identifier string, and a notice file asserts all rights reserved beside a permissive licence
projects.why_it_matters: The most complete worked example of hierarchy and schemas as the organising principle of a note vault, and a reminder that a widely installed tool can stop without its files becoming unreadable.

projects.name: Vibe Kanban
projects.description: Board application that ran several vendors' coding-agent tools as supervised processes, each in its own working tree, with approval gating and diff review.
projects.canonical_data: a working tree per task plus a local database of tasks, attempts, and execution processes
projects.current_repo_note: Archived on the maintainer's own published declaration rather than a platform flag: the readme carries a sunsetting banner and the company behind it announced its closure in April 2026. Its final release retired the board and issue flows to an export-only page, so the product a reader would install no longer does what its name describes, though the per-task working-tree runs remain. No successor is named, so the supersession status does not apply.
strengths: Approval is real machinery rather than prose, with a service interface that creates a tool approval and blocks until it is answered
One adapter per vendor drives nine different coding-agent tools as supervised processes, each isolated in its own working tree
Substantial correctness infrastructure for its size, with hundreds of tests, dozens of schema migrations, and workflows covering the interface, the server, and the desktop build
weaknesses: The company behind it announced its closure, and the last commit, release, and package publication all fall in the same week of April 2026
Its final change retired the board and issue flows the product is named for, leaving an export page in their place
A promised community continuation was announced but no commit has followed in the months since
projects.why_it_matters: Showed a task board as the surface for parallel agent work, with per-task working trees and blocking approvals, and then retired the board while the machinery beneath it stayed.

projects.name: pool
projects.description: Proprietary Poolside coding agent for the terminal that also runs as an ACP server inside editors and as an ACP client driving other agent servers.
projects.canonical_data: local working tree and Git worktree sessions, resumable session history and trajectory logs, and settings.yaml permissions, skills, and AGENTS.md instructions
projects.current_repo_note: The public repository carries documentation, a changelog, and third-party notices only; pool itself is distributed as a precompiled binary under Poolside's Terms of Use, so its GitHub metadata measures the distribution and issue-tracking repository rather than the agent's source.
strengths: Layered human control: four approval modes including a risk-classifying Auto mode, tool and path allow/deny rules merged across personal, project, and gitignored local scopes with deny winning, mandatory approval for subshells and piped commands, and a Plan mode that requires review to leave even under Allow all

First-class on both sides of the Agent Client Protocol, running as a server inside Zed, JetBrains, and Xcode and as a client driving Claude Agent, Codex, or a remote agent server, alongside MCP, AGENTS.md, and SKILL.md support

An optional Docker sandbox with read-only or read-write workspace mounts and a proxy-enforced egress allowlist, plus Git worktree sessions, mid-turn steering, rewind, resumable cross-directory sessions, and newline-delimited JSON output with distinct exit codes for pool exec
weaknesses: The agent ships only as a precompiled binary: the public repository holds documentation, a changelog, and dependency notices, the terms forbid reverse engineering, and no source is published for the loop, its tools, or the Auto-mode risk classifier

On the default Poolside-hosted path the terms permit using prompts, code, and output to train Poolside models unless the user opts out, making the vendor's own inference the weakest of the supported backends for confidential work

Young and still moving: fourteen releases reaching v1.0.16 since May 2026, Windows install in preview, pool acp serve marked experimental, and hooks that run without an approval prompt and fail open by documented design rather than acting as a security boundary
projects.why_it_matters: A rare coding agent that is a first-class ACP client as well as an ACP server, so one terminal interface can drive Poolside's own agent or someone else's while permissions, sandboxing, worktrees, and session handling stay on the client side.
